title: Finite-type and Noetherian geometry of the affine-line support pair
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$ with projection $p:X\to Y$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be the zero section, defined on each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset Y$ by the quotient $R[t]\to R$, $t\mapsto0$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $U=X\setminus s(Y)$ with its open subscheme structure and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion [def-weil-open-immersion]; over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ this is the principal open $\operatorname{Spec}(R[t]_t)$, also denoted $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,t^{-1}]$. Then $X$ and $U$ are of finite type over $k$, the three schemes $Y,X,U$ are Noetherian, and $j$ is quasi-compact. Here Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, with quasi-compactness of schemes and morphisms understood as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
